seeded_defect: Wrong layer / symptom patch. The root cause is in tinydb/queries.py Query.fragment: its hash tuple ('fragment', freeze(document)) omits self._path, so Query().home.fragment(f) and Query().work.fragment(f) are equal and hash-equal and collide in the query cache. Instead of adding the path to the hash, the PR adds Table._is_fragment_query in tinydb/table.py, which walks the private QueryInstance._hash structure and makes Table.search bypass the query cache (lookup and store) for every query that contains a fragment. Consequences: (1) the equality/hash bug the issue explicitly reports (`... == ...` returns True) is not fixed, so any other use of query equality/hashing (dict/set keys, user caches, custom Table subclasses, the LRU cache of code that doesn't go through search) is still wrong; (2) table.py now depends on the private hash-tuple layout of queries.py (layering violation: the query owns its identity, the table only trusts hash/eq and is_cacheable()); (3) all fragment queries silently lose caching, a performance/semantics change beyond the issue. search/count/get results are now correct, so existing suite, own tests and the first two hidden tests pass; hidden test test_fragment_queries_on_different_paths_are_not_equal fails.
detection_criterion: A blocking finding with category approach that says the fix belongs in Query.fragment's hash (the path must be part of the query identity) rather than in Table.search, and/or that fragment queries on different paths still compare/hash equal (the issue's own `==` example still returns True). Mentioning that table.py reaches into the private _hash of queries or that fragment caching is disabled supports it but alone is only partial credit. A finding categorised only as code that asks to also fix __eq__ counts as detected but mis-routed.
